I used to play Warframe normally—I have close to 5,000 hours of playtime there. I tried The First Descendant back when it was in its first beta, and at the time, I thought, "When this game comes out, I'll definitely play it," but the game has completely gone to ♥♥♥♥. I generally love grinding in games. To mention the pros of this game: the gameplay mechanics are nice, it looks visually great, and the boss fights are also good. The cons? They couldn't optimize it properly on the UE5 engine, and constantly running from place to place exhausts you (with endless loading screens, even though I have an M.2 SSD).

What I complain about the most is that I’m constantly farming, but I never feel like I’m getting any stronger. I keep checking the leaderboard, and it's always the same people whose weapons and mods are way, way superior to yours. Okay, I have nothing to say to that—those guys traded and got ahead of you, I have no problem with that. But that means the foundation is "pay-to-win." Now, you're going to say, "Bro, why don't you drop stuff and sell it too, then go buy mods and weapons and get strong yourself?" Bro, do you think I didn't try? I put the strongest thing I had up for sale both on the website and in-game, and not a peep from anyone.

Aside from all that, there is a disgusting situation in the chat. People writing things like, "I want to eat the feet of the character Valby/Ine[s]", "I want to drink the bathwater of the character Ultimate Bunny/Viessa", or saying they want to do this and that to certain characters. Let me give you an example: say I insulted someone and got banned from the server (by the way, I've never been banned from the game, I'm just giving this as an example). Meanwhile, another guy writes all sorts of bath and foot-fetish stuff with various characters, and why don't they get banned? They're causing chat pollution, it's a bizarre situation.

Additionally, none of the characters in the game are balanced—you have to play whatever is in the meta. I have no problem with a meta existing, but don't exaggerate the percentages to this extent. For example, I want to play Ajax, but Ajax can't deal damage—it's a comical, ridiculous situation. There is no balancing among the characters.

Fundamentally, the game brings new areas and new things, which is fine. But these new areas make you feel like you still can't deal damage, like you're still not strong. In other words, the enemies are absolute damage sponges; you hit them, they just soak up the damage and refuse to die :D

To sum it up briefly: if you want to play this game, unless you have a job, a girlfriend, and a life, it's tailor-made for you. Because the game demands that you grind like you have no life. Nexon isn't doing this for the first time; they are slowly ruining their other games the exact same way. If you just want to see some memes and ass in a game, you can play something else—at least you'd get a better result.

I didn't expect this to happen, but after a streak of high-quality monthly updates, TFD is actually finally a very good game.

Most of the reworked characters, their modules, and weapons are equally strong. New playable content is being added consistently. On top of that, there are regular events with, to be honest, pretty good free cosmetics.

Since some of the older parts of the game have been simplified and progression streamlined, I suppose the new player experience is also better. Especially when combined with pity systems and the built-in library, so you almost never have to open Google to search for where what drops etc.

Overall, it's a fun to play looter shooter.
